notes: Written, not yet run against a model. Copy evals/files/ into the root of an empty scratch git repository and commit it before each case. Every case carries the 'lifecycle' tag; 'negative' cases check that nothing is written.

evals.name: trivial-decision-writes-nothing
evals.prompt: Write an ADR for naming the rate limit module rate_limit.py instead of throttle.py. It is in docs/plans/api-rate-limit.md.
evals.expected_output: Applies the significance test, finds the naming decision easy to reverse and unsurprising, writes nothing, and says where the information belongs instead.
expectations: States that the decision fails the significance test, naming at least "hard to reverse" as the failed part
Creates no file under docs/adr/ and leaves docs/adr/README.md unchanged
Says in one or two sentences where the information belongs instead (for example the plan or a commit message)
Does not invent a stronger rationale to make the decision qualify

evals.name: record-significant-decision
evals.prompt: Record an ADR for the in-process token bucket decision in docs/plans/api-rate-limit.md.
evals.expected_output: Writes docs/adr/0002 for the token bucket with the rejected Redis alternative, status accepted, the decider and source, and adds it to the index without touching ADR 0001.
expectations: Applies the three-part significance test and states the result for each part
Creates docs/adr/0002-<kebab-title>.md, numbered after the existing 0001
The ADR has status accepted, a date, and names the decider from the plan (user, Q-03)
Considered options name the shared Redis counter as the rejected alternative with its reason
Consequences include that limits are per instance and multiply with instances
Links the source plan
Adds one line for 0002 to docs/adr/README.md
Does not modify docs/adr/0001-store-sessions-in-postgres.md
Does not commit

evals.name: supersede-changes-only-old-status
evals.prompt: We decided today to move sessions out of Postgres into the cache cluster: session reads now dominate database load. The rejected option was keeping Postgres with a read replica, because replica lag breaks logout. Supersede ADR 0001.
evals.expected_output: Writes 0002 superseding 0001, changes only the status line of 0001, and updates both index entries.
expectations: Creates docs/adr/0002-<kebab-title>.md with status accepted and a "Supersedes: 0001" link
Names the read-replica option as rejected, with replica lag breaking logout as the reason
In 0001, changes only the status line, to 'superseded by 0002'; the rest of the file is byte-identical
Updates docs/adr/README.md so 0001 shows superseded and 0002 is listed

evals.name: standard-practice-is-not-an-adr
evals.prompt: Make an ADR saying we return 429 with a Retry-After header when a client is over the limit.
evals.expected_output: Declines because returning 429 with Retry-After is standard HTTP behaviour, so it is not surprising, and no real alternative was weighed.
expectations: States that the decision fails "surprising without context" and has no real rejected alternative in the plan
Writes no ADR file and does not edit the index
Offers to write it if the author names a real alternative that was considered, without inventing one

evals.name: extract-from-plan-returns-drafts-only
evals.prompt: You are called by plan-sweep in extract-from-plan mode for docs/plans/api-rate-limit.md. Return draft ADRs for its candidates.
evals.expected_output: Checks both candidates against the code, returns one draft for the token bucket, declines the module name, and writes no files.
expectations: Checks the token bucket claim against src/rate_limit.py and cites it
Returns one draft ADR, for the in-process token bucket, numbered 0002
Declines the module-name candidate with the failed significance test
Writes no files; the drafts are returned to the caller
